import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_5.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and their types (for reference)
target_columns = [
    'S/N', 
    'Building/Project Name', 
    'Street Name', 
    'Postal District', 
    'Type', 
    'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)', 
    'Monthly Gross Rent($)', 
    'Floor Area (sq ft)', 
    'Lease Commencement Date'
]

# Function to clean and standardize each dataframe to match target schema and types
def clean_source_df(df):
    # 1. Ensure all target columns exist (all source tables have the same schema)
    df = df[target_columns].copy()

    # 2. Data type conversions and cleaning:

    # 'S/N' as integer
    df['S/N'] = pd.to_numeric(df['S/N'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # 'Building/Project Name' as string, strip whitespace
    df['Building/Project Name'] = df['Building/Project Name'].astype(str).str.strip()

    # 'Street Name' as string, strip whitespace
    df['Street Name'] = df['Street Name'].astype(str).str.strip()

    # 'Postal District' as integer
    df['Postal District'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Postal District'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # 'Type' as string, strip whitespace
    df['Type'] = df['Type'].astype(str).str.strip()

    # 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)' as string
    # Some values like 'na*' exist, convert all to string and strip
    df['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'] = df['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'].astype(str).str.strip()

    # 'Monthly Gross Rent($)' as integer
    df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # 'Floor Area (sq ft)' as string, strip whitespace
    df['Floor Area (sq ft)'] = df['Floor Area (sq ft)'].astype(str).str.strip()

    # 'Lease Commencement Date' as string, strip whitespace
    df['Lease Commencement Date'] = df['Lease Commencement Date'].astype(str).str.strip()

    return df

# Read, clean, and collect all source dataframes
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0, dtype=str)  # read all as string first to avoid dtype issues
    df_clean = clean_source_df(df)
    dfs.append(df_clean)

# Since all source tables have exactly the same schema as the target,
# we can safely concatenate (union) all rows
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Optional: sort by 'S/N' ascending to mimic target examples order (not mandatory)
target_df = target_df.sort_values(by='S/N').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
